propers.name: Lesson
propers.text:
Haec dicit Dominus Deus: Si abstuleris de medio tui catenam, et desieris
extendere digitum, et loqui quod non prodest. Cum effuderis esurienti animam
tuam, et animam afflictam repleveris, orietur in tenebris lux tua, et tenebrae
tuae erunt sicut meridies. Et requiem tibi dabit Dominus semper, et implebit
splendoribus animam tuam, et ossa tua liberabit, et eris quasi hortus irriguus,
et sicut fons aquarum, cujus non deficient aquae. Et aedificabuntur in te
deserta saeculorum: fundamenta generationis et generationis suscitabis: et
vocaberis aedificator sepium, avertens semitas in quietem. Si averteris a
sabbato pedem tuum, facere voluntatem tuam in die sancto meo, et vocaveris
sabbatum delicatum, et sanctum Domini gloriosum, et glorificaveris eum, dum non
facis vias tuas, et non invenitur voluntas tua, ut loquaris sermonem: tunc
delectaberis super Domino: et sustollam te super altitudines terrae, et cibabo
te hereditate Jacob patris tui. Os enim Domini locutum est.

The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1962 prints the conclusion written out (14 words); the public-domain witnesses abbreviate it to the short cue; 1862 text layer damages 6 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: suscipe domine -> d mine; uoluisti dignanter -> uolufsti digndnter; placari presta quesumus -> plac ri pnesta qu tsumusi; operatione mundati beneplacitum -> operatio ne munddti beneplacituni; nostre -> nostne; offeramus affectum -> offerdmus affe ctum per d minum ali; 1922 Mame text layer damages 4 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): suscipe -> (absent from the aligned window); immolatione -> immolati ne; quesumus -> queesumus; operatione -> operatiene; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 80, artifact PDF p. 194; the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer. Recorded limitation: The day was identified by the facsimile's own running head (Sabbato post cineres) and by the station heading that opens the formulary, and this oration is the first Secreta the Missal prints inside that day's Mass, taken after that day's Ant. ad Introitum and before the next day's station heading; the marginal number was read on the page image. Every 1862 reading in this entry rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone - this repository holds no page images for its temporal run - so where that layer damages a word the letterforms are inferred from the 1922 Mame at the same place rather than read. Not checked: the Oratio super populum that the 1962 prints after this Mass's Postcommunion (not on this work list), the 1604 and the 1570, and whether the 1862 also prints this prayer elsewhere in its book.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
